R439 — CPU service diagnostic concurrency and lifetime audit
Date: 2026-10-14
Result: source-only review of the arrived implementation. No changes, builds, tests, AST runs, GPU/process/environment/log/state-JSON reads, or Git mutations were performed. This is not a dynamic race or sanitizer qualification.

Reviewed source
Candidate S: /home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/diag-decode-service-budget-20261014
Implementation report: R/implementation-decode-service-cpu-budget-v1.txt
Key files: src/kernels/cpu/pool.cpp, include/strata/kernels/cpu/pool.hpp, include/strata/kernels/cpu/service_budget.hpp, src/core/expert_source.cpp, src/program/generate.cpp, src/core/verify.cpp.
The request-scoped flag is created at generate.cpp:9685-9690 and explicitly finished at 10449-10450 after the final commit wait at 10445. The ordinary verifier invokes the pool callback synchronously at verify.cpp:1595-1597 after its layer ring; the separately serviced path is verify.cpp:2633-2635. The diagnostic admission predicate excludes pipelined/staged cases.

Findings

1. Raw service_budget_ pointer: source establishes phase-to-worker and worker-to-issuer ordering.
DispatchServiceScope::counter() installs the pointer at expert_source.cpp:1513-1517. That constructor runs before the dispatch body (1962-1966), which reaches run_split_multi_native. The pool writes phase metadata and mode before begin_batch; begin_batch stores packed head with release and publishes an epoch, while workers load epoch with acquire before leaving park (pool.cpp:243-254; worker loop at 190-228). A worker therefore cannot read the newly installed pointer or current phase metadata before publication. The host inline drain reads the same pointer on the issuer thread.

Each successful drain claim records task/call counters before done_.fetch_add(release) at pool.cpp:320-386. The issuer waits for done with acquire at 278-298, then wait_parked loads parked_ with acquire at 257-275. Each returning worker performs parked_.fetch_add(acq_rel) after its drain at 225-228. This final parked boundary makes the per-slot writes visible and guarantees no worker still uses the pointer when run_phase returns. The next phase does not overwrite mode/rows/head until its own pre-phase wait_parked; the prior phase also returns only after post-phase wait_parked (390-409). A claim rejected for a stale epoch or exhausted index exits before instrumentation/task recording (claim at 232-240; drain at 301-305); it cannot create a delayed write. The pool's pre-existing epoch-bearing claim prevents a late sleeper from claiming a later batch.

The serialized native dispatch scope unbinds with service_budget(nullptr) only after the pool call returns (expert_source.cpp:1523-1527). This is after the last parked boundary. Its destructor body then completes while the request mutex is still held; its ServiceClockScope member is destroyed before the mutex member, so the issuer dispatch receipt is finalized before request close can acquire that mutex. The non-atomic pointer use therefore has a valid publisher/consumer lifetime in the eligible synchronous path. This relies on the existing pool contract that callers do not mutate the pointer during a pool call; the setter comment in pool.hpp says the same.

2. Slot ownership and unsynchronized fields match the actual writers.
NativeServiceBudget documents slot 0 as issuer and worker id i as slot i+1 (service_budget.hpp:64-78). Pool drain passes id=-1 for inline host work and a stable nonnegative worker id for each worker. Every worker thread owns its own slot throughout all phases; only that thread increments that slot's task and call counters. The issuer owns slot 0, including the serial intermediate quantization at pool.cpp:509-518. The issuer alone updates planned_tasks, phase counters, pool.invalid, and dispatch-level counts while holding the request state mutex. NativeServiceBudget::complete and final aggregation occur after acquiring that same mutex in finish, after no dispatch remains (expert_source.cpp:1557-1570). No per-slot atomic is needed under these observed ownership and join/barrier rules.

For a successful task, task(id, ...) and all call-scope destructors execute before the worker increments done. For each phase, run_phase brackets parked-before, publish-through-done, and done-through-parked on the issuer and completes all three before returning (pool.cpp:390-409). Empty or failed claims do not increment task counts. complete() checks slot bounds, task sums against planned tasks, and equal boundary receipt counts (service_budget.hpp:80 onward). The fixed 129-slot allocation covers the accepted maximum of 128 workers: IDs 0..127 map to slots 1..128; eligibility rejects a larger worker count before binding (expert_source.cpp:1536-1541).

3. Close, exceptions, and callback lifetime.
The observer binding is a shared_ptr protected by service_binding_mutex. Each dispatch first copies that shared_ptr while holding the binding mutex, releases it, then takes the request state mutex (expert_source.cpp:1501-1522). Request finish clears the published shared_ptr while holding only the binding mutex, releases it, then takes the state mutex and marks inactive (1550-1562). These are sequential acquisitions, not a nested reverse lock order. A dispatcher that copied the observer before unbind keeps it alive and either completes before close takes the state mutex, or enters afterward and sees active=false under that mutex; in the latter case it does not bind the pool pointer or touch counters. A dispatcher starting after unbind sees no observer. There is no use-after-free path from the observer pointer in this sequence.

The generation scope destructor calls finish(error_or_early_exit, 0) if an early return or exception bypasses explicit close. DispatchServiceScope is stack-local in the callback, so ordinary C++ stack unwinding first unbinds the pool pointer and finalizes its issuer scope before the generation scope can close. The wrapper callback calls expert_pool_dispatch_multi synchronously; Verifier::run calls it directly at the layer ring and does not enqueue it as a deferred CPU callback. For ordinary verification, the subsequent commit wait precedes request finish. The verifier's error-drain guard synchronizes compute and copy streams before returning on an error (verify.cpp:1472-1481). Thus the reviewed path has no late CPU callback remaining at request close. An abort/terminate from existing stall/fault paths is process termination, not a continuing diagnostic owner.

If a future code path changes the pool callback to deferred/asynchronous execution, it must join/drain that callback before request finish; current source provides no separate callback reference count. Do not generalize this review to such a future path.

4. No concrete deadlock or undefined access found in the reviewed path.
The relevant locks are service_binding_mutex and the per-request state mutex. Observer lookup and finish do not hold both simultaneously; dispatch holds only the request mutex for its callback and does not acquire the binding mutex in its destructor. Pool workers use neither mutex. Pool waits remain the pre-existing spin/stall/abort protocol. Service counter writes are per-thread, and close waits on the same state mutex after dispatch scope has released it. No lock cycle, duplicate slot writer, out-of-range worker slot, or worker access after unbind was found.

A measurement caveat, not a concurrency defect: ServiceClockScope writes a slot's receipt in its destructor. In the issuer dispatch scope this destructor runs after the scope destructor body has already unbound the pool pointer; however, it still runs while the request mutex and its shared state are alive. This is safe and close cannot aggregate until it completes.

Off-path behavior
With no service observer bound, service_observer returns empty and ServiceClockScope receives null counters; its constructor/destructor then make no wall/CPU clock reads and do not update counters (service_budget.hpp:45-60). Source inspection supports zero diagnostic clock calls and no added atomic operations on the off path. It does not prove zero instruction/performance overhead from branches or the per-dispatch observer lookup; that needs Main's planned off/on measurement.

Required qualification
The source argument is internally coherent, but the integration fixture, host ASan/UBSan, full builds, existing pool tests, and no-new/ordinary decode checks listed in the implementation report remain unrun here. Main should run its own existing recipe and preserve the fixture's assertions with NDEBUG disabled. Dynamic checks should cover worker delays/sleep wakeup, request early-return/exception close, exact emitted route counts, clock failures, and normal completion; exercise the existing epoch protocol under the small-spin test setting. Keep the current stock bench untouched during this audit.

Erratum for R437
R437's “Not proposed” sentence reversed the R436 outcomes. Correct values: paired GU NT1 was −3.76%, paired GU NT8 was +2.31%, and gather NT1 was +17.57% (slower); these were isolated synthetic results, not model-level performance. R436 was not modified.
